chapter_seo_title: Dao Twisted World Ch 283: Li Huowang Hears a Voice That Breaks His Calm
chapter_meta_description: An auditory hallucination shatters Li Huowang’s fragile peace. In a quiet chapter of dread and self-revelation, he confronts the Black Tai Sui—and a masked visitor.
og_title: The Voice Returns: Li Huowang’s Night of Dread
og_description: Under Kongming lanterns and a starry sky, the Dao-Twisted World’s most fragile Heart-Element faces his greatest fear: a single garbled word that might not be real.
twitter_title: He Thought He Was Fine. Then He Heard a Voice.
twitter_description: A quiet night in Yinling City turns into a slow-burn descent into doubt. Li Huowang discovers even Black Tai Sui can’t silence hope—or dread.

lore_anchors.definition: Small paper hot-air balloons traditionally released during festivals or as memorials for the dead, named after the strategist Zhuge Liang. In this chapter, they carry family surnames and are used as a funeral rite.
A pre-modern Chinese profession where a man patrols the streets with a bamboo clapper and gong, announcing the time and warning of fire. The fourth watch signals the deepest hour of the night.
A rare human constitution in the Dao-Twisted World that makes the bearer unable to distinguish reality from hallucination; their beliefs can literally reshape reality.
A grotesque parasitic entity used by Li Huowang to suppress his hallucinatory episodes; its flesh contains substances that stabilize his mind.
A traditional Chinese folk performance mask depicting an oversized, laughing child’s face; used in celebratory dances. In this novel, it is repurposed as a sinister disguise.
